focus: Which router copies a gate holds equal, and which drift unchecked
keyFindings: Three routing implementations are genuinely held equal. differential.py lifts the pseudocode out of router-contract.md, executes it as a module, and compares route_contract.py to it on five guards: prose-table subset, copy parity, table parity, behavior parity over 220 corpus inputs, and corpus coverage of every command, false prefix, topic and shape. It also requires the kernel to carry exactly one python fence and holds that block byte-equal, then AST-equal, to the pseudocode minus comments. Fix: none; this is the one sound routing gate. Only the kernel's code is gated, not its routing prose: copy parity compares Section 11 and checks that Section 11 is reachable from the kernel and from routing.md, but nothing compares Sections 2 and 7 to that code or to each other, so the always-loaded prose can instruct behaviour the router no longer has while every guard stays green. Fix: claude project/Custom Instructions.md sections 2 and 7. The two leaf maps are validated by different gates that never compare them: ROUTER.md's RESOURCE_MAP is held by the skilled root-router contract for on-disk resolution and leaf-manifest registration, while router-contract.md's RESOURCE_MAP is held by differential's table parity against route_contract.py. Either map can change which leaf an intent loads without the other gate noticing, which is why the CLICK_UP and FIGMA lanes can exist in one map only. Fix: compare the two maps, or delete one. Fix: benchmark/gates/check_hub.py and benchmark/hub-routing-cases.json. The FLOW lane escapes table parity: differential compares RESOURCE_MAP lanes for TASK, BUG, DOC, STORY and INTERACTIVE only, and its coverage guard never routes a Flow intent, so the Flow pair and the figjam packet's type routes have no executable contract. The figjam packet is self-consistent, but nothing holds its type table, its route_flow() and the hub ROUTER.md together. Fix: add FLOW to the compared lanes or state why it is out. The staging spec names sk-create-figjam/ROUTER.md as a router copy to compare, but no such file exists, and check_hub fails the build if one appears because ROUTER.md is in its packet-residue list. The figjam routing copy is its SKILL.md Section 2 plus its route_flow pseudocode. Recorded so the question is not answered against a phantom file. The router-contract ALWAYS lane names sk-product-owner/SKILL.md, a path its own load guard can never load because the inventory is packet-relative; differential works around it by filtering the entry out before comparing lanes. The inconsistency is tolerated by the gate rather than fixed, so a second such entry would also pass. Fix: router-contract.md line 137-141. Coverage by surface, which is the direct answer to this question: intent routing inside sk-product-owner is fully gated across three implementations; hub stage one is gated only by 37 gold rows against a replica; the stage-two leaf map has its paths gated but its intent-to-leaf equality ungated; figjam type routing is ungated; kernel routing prose is ungated while kernel routing code is byte-gated. Fix: the three ungated rows need a gate each, and the two Leaf Maps need one comparison. ruledOut: Counting the gold-row replay as a stage-one specification gate: it tests a replica against expectations, not the prose against the replica
Treating the differential corpus group named known-divergences as an exemption: compare_input applies to every corpus input with no exception list, so those two entries must now agree
Treating sk-create-figjam/ROUTER.md as an existing copy: the file is absent and a hub gate forbids it
